A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same homogeneous cryo-EM reconstruction work, renamed from CryoGS to CryoSplat. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on four EMPIAR datasets, including FSC results, runtime measurements, Gaussian-count ablations, and appendix memory and isotropy comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original reconstruction experiments and quantitative and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: CryoGS is renamed CryoSplat. The anisotropic GMM, normalized orthographic projection, FFT alignment, tile-based rasterization, initialization, and MSE objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate homogeneous reconstruction on EMPIAR-10028, EMPIAR-10049, EMPIAR-10076, and EMPIAR-10180 using published particle poses. Appendix A retains the same dataset descriptions and populations.

E2.justification: Backprojection and CryoDRGN remain the evaluated baselines in the reconstruction, runtime, and memory comparisons. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain the same image resolutions, published poses and CTF parameters, half-dataset FSC evaluation with a 0.143 threshold, Gaussian-count configurations, and training budgets of five GMM epochs versus 50 CryoDRGN epochs.

E4.justification: The Gaussian-count analysis in Figure 3 and Figure S2, convergence comparisons in Figure 2, and isotropic-versus-anisotropic analysis in Figure S1 are retained with the same settings and findings.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, specified random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reporting practices and half-map FSC procedure are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 2 retains the proposed method's resolutions of 3.80, 2.49, 3.30, and 4.26 Å on the four datasets, respectively. Baseline results, runtime values, Table S1 memory measurements, and appendix qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The image-formation assumptions, Gaussian definitions and projection derivations in Equations (1)–(14), and FSC formula in Appendix B are unchanged. No formal reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same novelty and contribution claims concerning reconstruction from random initialization, physically accurate projection, computational efficiency, and reconstruction quality. Renaming the method does not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of robustness, Gaussian capacity, anisotropy, and efficiency remain unchanged. Both explicitly require known poses and leave ab initio and heterogeneous reconstruction to future work.

D1.justification: The preprocessing instructions, initialization values, Adam settings, RTX 3090 hardware disclosure, and Appendix C implementation explanations are retained. Both state that code will be released upon publication.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to prior GMM reconstruction methods, neural representations, and 3D Gaussian Splatting.

P1.justification: CryoGS/cryoGS is systematically renamed CryoSplat/cryoSplat in the title, headings, and prose, and the version/date header changes. The narrative wording and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure labels, legends, captions, and Table S1 adopt the new method name, with small panel-sizing, positioning, and text-flow adjustments. Figures 1–4, S1–S2, and Table S1 retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: v2 changes the method name and makes minor presentation adjustments while retaining the same method, evidence, mathematical exposition, reproducibility information, and limitations. These edits establish no meaningful overall quality gain or decline.
